sources.title: Just Arrived – Catalán para principiantes
sources.publisher: Servei de Llengües i Terminologia, Universitat Politècnica de Catalunya (UPC)
sources.summary: Slide deck for a two-session taster course. Spanish explanations with Catalan examples: introductions (dir-se, ser), greetings, Romance-language intercomprehension (Catalan vs. Italian/French/Portuguese/Romanian), alphabet and syllable-splitting digraphs, days and months, numbers 1–100, definite articles and noun gender, countries with de/d'/del, nationality adjectives, and facts about Catalan (speakers, territories, use at university). Several slides are images only; days, numbers and the alphabet were read from page renders.

sources.title: Les meves primeres paraules en català / Mis primeras palabras en español
sources.publisher: Servei de Llengües i Terminologia, UPC (with the support of the Generalitat de Catalunya)
sources.summary: Guide for language mentors (Barcelona, December 2019). Five units, each a mock situation with speech bubbles and word lists: 1 meeting for coffee (name, origin, age, studies, languages, phone, address, likes); 2 shopping at the market and for clothes; 3 cinema and plans (time, days, film genres); 4 looking for a flat and asking for directions; 5 university life. Each unit has 'Cal tenir en compte!' pronunciation and usage notes and 'Aprofundim' culture notes. Pages 3–13 are Catalan; pages 14–24 repeat them in Spanish, which is where the es translations come from.

sources.title: Lèxic bàsic d'arquitectura tècnica
sources.publisher: Servei de Llengües i Terminologia, UPC; Servei de Publicacions de la UPC
sources.summary: Catalan–Spanish and Spanish–Catalan glossary of building and architecture terms (about 300 entries with grammatical category), compiled with students of the EUPB. It ends with a list of SI symbols and abbreviations. Authors: Joan Albiol, Jeroni Vinyet, Montserrat Noró, Anna Cervera. Only its metadata and a handful of everyday words (plug, pavement, ceiling, step, landing, table…) were extracted.

sources.title: Català Bàsic 2 – Materials per a les sessions presencials
sources.publisher: Servei de Llengües i Terminologia, UPC (author: Maria Pardo)
sources.summary: Teacher guide and student handouts for the classroom sessions of a blended A2.1 course built on Parla.cat (Barcelona, December 2018). Sessions cover housing (song 'Qualsevol nit pot sortir el sol', flat-share role plays, furniture, describing your city using a text about Kraków), jobs and work conditions, illness at the pharmacy, biographies and past events (passat perifràstic), the shopping list, food and recipes (Blaumut's song 'Pa amb oli i sal'), and the festa major. Pages 27–32 list the grammar, vocabulary and culture syllabus of Parla.cat Bàsic 2, units 1–7. The level is above A1, so its grammar entries mark later-stage targets.

sources.title: Conversem? Activitats de suport a l'aprenentatge de català inicial fora de l'aula
sources.publisher: Serveis lingüístics universitaris; coordinated by Jordi Pujol (SLT, UPC) and Josep M. Boladeras (Institut de Llengües, Universitat de Lleida)
sources.summary: Seven conversation-practice cards for mentors and beginner learners (Barcelona–Lleida, September 2016): 1 Fem un cafè? (introductions), 2 Anem a casa (directions, family), 3 Parlem per telèfon, 4 tourism (opening hours, proposals, preferences), 5 Coneixem la universitat, 6 Anem al cine, 7 Comprem al mercat. Each card has numbered model exchanges in informal (a) and formal (b) versions, word lists, verb tables and pronunciation notes. It uses the spelling in force before 2017 (sóc, dóna, véns); the other sources use soc.

sources.title: El Petit Príncep (Catalan translation of Antoine de Saint-Exupéry, Le Petit Prince)
sources.copyright: Copyrighted translation. Do not quote it in lessons or copy any sentences or passages.
sources.summary: A literary text (about 15,000 words) used ONLY for word frequency. The top-level 'frequency' array lists its 300 most frequent lowercase word forms, generated by build-frequency.mjs. No sentences, phrases or passages from it were copied into this dataset.

phrases.pl: Nie, nie ma jej. Wiesz, kiedy wróci? Nie, nie wiem!

phrases.ca: Hola, volia saber quant val el lloguer del pis cada mes.
phrases.pl: Dzień dobry, chciałem/chciałam zapytać, ile wynosi miesięczny czynsz za mieszkanie.

phrases.ca: Un moment, que t'ho miro.
phrases.pl: Chwileczkę, sprawdzę ci to.

phrases.ca: Em pots dir el teu número de telèfon o la teva adreça de correu electrònic?
phrases.pl: Możesz mi podać swój numer telefonu albo adres e-mail?

phrases.ca: Et convido a berenar!
phrases.pl: Zapraszam cię na podwieczorek!

phrases.ca: Jo vull xocolata amb xurros! Doncs, jo també.
phrases.pl: Ja chcę czekoladę z churros! No to ja też.

phrases.ca: Quin horari feu? De 10 a 14 h i a la tarda de 17 h a 20 h.
phrases.pl: W jakich godzinach jesteście otwarci? Od 10 do 14 i po południu od 17 do 20.

phrases.ca: Quins dies de la setmana obriu? De dimarts a dissabte.
phrases.pl: W które dni tygodnia jest otwarte? Od wtorku do soboty.

phrases.ca: Avui és obert? Al matí sí, a la tarda és tancat.
phrases.pl: Czy dziś jest otwarte? Rano tak, po południu zamknięte.

phrases.ca: A quina hora tanqueu al matí? A les 14 h.
phrases.pl: O której zamykacie przed południem? O 14.

phrases.ca: Quant val l'entrada? Val 3 € per persona. / És gratuïta.
phrases.pl: Ile kosztuje wstęp? 3 euro od osoby. / Jest bezpłatny.

phrases.ca: Feu visites guiades? En quines llengües?
phrases.pl: Prowadzicie zwiedzanie z przewodnikiem? W jakich językach?

phrases.ca: Et ve de gust anar a visitar la Seu Vella?
phrases.pl: Masz ochotę zwiedzić Seu Vella?

phrases.ca: Què et sembla si anem a veure l'actuació castellera?

phrases.ca: Oi tant que sí! / Bona idea!

phrases.pl: Chcesz zwiedzić Sagrada Família? Nie, bo byłem/byłam tam w zeszłym tygodniu.

phrases.ca: T'estimes més anar a la platja o a la muntanya?

phrases.ca: Amb qui hi anirem? Hi anirem amb la meva companya de pis.

phrases.pl: Tak, wiem. Bardzo dziękuję.

phrases.ca: Tens targeta client?
phrases.pl: Masz kartę stałego klienta?

phrases.ca: Tingui, el canvi.
phrases.pl: Proszę, reszta.

phrases.ca: Bé, me la quedo.
phrases.pl: Dobrze, biorę ją.

phrases.ca: Tingui el tiquet per si l'ha de canviar.
phrases.pl: Proszę paragon, gdyby trzeba było wymienić.

phrases.ca: Casa meva és casa vostra.
phrases.pl: Mój dom jest waszym domem.

phrases.pl: Kto mieszka na statku? Myślę, że na statku mieszka Sindbad.

grammar.title: Verb dir-se (present)
grammar.rule: dir-se ('to be called') is a reflexive verb: the pronoun goes before the verb.

examples.ca: Com et dius? Em dic Marc.
examples.pl: Jak masz na imię? Mam na imię Marc.

grammar.title: Verb ser (present)
grammar.rule: ser ('to be') is used for identity and origin. The source uses the 2017 spelling 'soc'; Conversem (2016) writes 'sóc'.

examples.ca: Soc la Martina! I tu, qui ets?
examples.pl: Jestem Martina! A ty, kim jesteś?

grammar.title: Personal article before names
grammar.rule: Catalan puts a definite article before people's names: el/en for male names, la for female names, and l' before a vowel ('l'Aina', 'l'Enric'). Exception: 'la' stays before unstressed i/hi, e.g. 'la Isabel'.

grammar.title: Definite articles
grammar.rule: Singular el / la become l' before a vowel or h. Plurals are els and les. Exceptions: la universitat, la Isabel (unstressed i/u).

grammar.title: Gender and number of nouns
grammar.rule: Feminine nouns usually add -a and plurals add -s. Feminine -a becomes -es in the plural.

examples.ca: el director, la directora, els directors, les directores

grammar.title: de + article with countries
grammar.rule: 'Soc de' + country. 'de' becomes d' before a vowel and merges with the article: de + el = del, de + els = dels. 'de la', 'de l'' and 'de les' don't merge.

grammar.title: Nationality adjectives: gender
grammar.rule: Masculine ending in a consonant: add -a (suec/sueca). Masculine ending in a stressed vowel -à/-è/-í/-ó: feminine -ana/-ena/-ina/-ona (mexicà/mexicana). -ès becomes -esa (polonès/polonesa). Language names are usually the same as the masculine nationality.

forms.consonant: suec → sueca, turc → turca, espanyol → espanyola
forms.-à/-è/-í/-ó: mexicà → mexicana, eslovè → eslovena, argentí → argentina, letó → letona

grammar.title: Digraphs that split or stay together across syllables
grammar.rule: When dividing into syllables, rr, l·l, ss, tx and ix are split (ter-ra, pel-lí-cu-la). ny, qu, gu and ll stay together.

grammar.title: Possessives
grammar.rule: Possessive = article + possessive form, which agrees with the thing owned. The source misprints the vosaltres and ells rows ('les vostres' twice, 'el seus'); the correct forms are shown here.

forms.jo: el meu, la meva, els meus, les meves
forms.tu: el teu, la teva, els teus, les teves
forms.ell/ella/vostè: el seu, la seva, els seus, les seves
forms.nosaltres: el nostre, la nostra, els nostres, les nostres
forms.vosaltres: el vostre, la vostra, els vostres, les vostres
forms.ells/elles/vostès: el seu, la seva, els seus, les seves

examples.ca: Et presento el Jordi, el meu company de pis.
És la Maria, la meva amiga.

grammar.title: casa + possessive after the noun
grammar.rule: With 'casa' the possessive comes after the noun and has no article: casa meva, casa teva, casa seva.

grammar.title: Interrogative quin / quina / quins / quines
grammar.rule: 'quin' ('which/what') agrees in gender and number with the noun that follows.

grammar.title: agradar: agrada / agraden
grammar.rule: 'agradar' works like the Polish 'podobać się': it agrees with the thing liked. Use the singular with an infinitive or singular noun and the plural with a plural noun. The person who likes it is an indirect-object pronoun (m', t', li…).

grammar.title: quant / quanta / quants / quantes
grammar.rule: 'quant' asks 'how much / how many' and agrees with the noun. 'Quant val?' means 'How much is it?'.

grammar.title: Indefinite articles
grammar.rule: un, una, uns, unes ('a/an, some').

grammar.title: Adjective gender
grammar.rule: Most adjectives add -a in the feminine. Final -t can become -d (gruixut → gruixuda) and -c becomes -g (groc → groga). Final -u becomes -va (blau → blava). Some forms don't change (taronja, rosa, lila, gran).

forms.-a: llarg → llarga, curt → curta, verd → verda

examples.ca: M'agrada més la verda, perquè és més llarga.
examples.pl: Bardziej podoba mi się zielona, bo jest dłuższa.

grammar.title: Demonstratives
grammar.rule: aquest… (near the speaker) and aquell… (far away). Both agree in gender and number. 'això' is the neuter form ('this thing').

grammar.title: Ordinal numbers
grammar.rule: Abbreviations: 1r primer, 2n segon, 3r tercer, 4t quart, 5è cinquè. Feminine forms: 1a primera, 2a segona, 3a tercera, 4a quarta.

grammar.title: Prepositions of time and range
grammar.rule: Ranges: de … a, des de … fins a. 'Up to': fins a.

forms.des de…fins a: des de les 9 fins a les 13

examples.ca: Tens classe cada dia? Sí, al matí, de 9 h a 13 h.
examples.pl: Masz zajęcia codziennie? Tak, rano, od 9 do 13.

examples.ca: Fins a quina hora és oberta la universitat?

grammar.title: Telling the time (quarts system)
grammar.rule: Whole hours: la una, les dues, les tres… Quarters count towards the NEXT hour: un quart d'una (12:15), dos quarts d'una (12:30), tres quarts d'una (12:45). Pronunciation note: 'A quina hora…?' sounds like 'aquinora'.

examples.ca: A quina hora quedem? A les dotze.
examples.pl: O której się spotykamy? O dwunastej.

grammar.title: Silent letters and other pronunciation notes
grammar.rule: h is silent. Final -r of infinitives (parlar, estudiar…) is silent, as is final -r in carrer, primer, tercer. Both final consonants are pronounced in ets, visc, tinc, anys, cinc. ç sounds like s (Barça). After a vowel, ix sounds like the 'sh' in English 'shellfish' (conèixer). The pronoun ho is pronounced 'u'. 'll' in 'vull' is often pronounced like 'i'.

grammar.title: l·l (ela geminada) vs ll
grammar.rule: l·l (pel·lícula, tranquil·la, excel·lent) is a slightly lengthened l. ll (llibre, vermella, dilluns) is a palatal sound, like Italian 'gli' or Portuguese 'lh'.

grammar.title: tu vs vostè
grammar.rule: Using 'tu' is the norm, even with teachers and doctors. 'vostè' (3rd person verb) is kept for very formal situations. Conversem gives every model exchange in an informal (tu) and a formal (vostè) version.

examples.ca: Et presento el Jordi. / Li presento el Jordi.

grammar.title: Regular -ar verbs (present)
grammar.rule: First conjugation (parlar, estudiar, treballar, quedar…): stem + -o, -es, -a, -em, -eu, -en.

grammar.title: Verb tenir (present)
grammar.rule: Used for age (tinc 13 anys), possession and feelings such as tinc set, tinc gana and tinc son.

grammar.title: Verb fer (present)
grammar.rule: fer = 'to do/make'. Used in 'Quin curs fas?', 'Fa fred', 'Quina talla fas?' and 'Quina pel·lícula fan?'.

examples.pl: Na którym jesteś roku? Na drugim.

grammar.title: Verb viure (present)
grammar.rule: Irregular 1st person 'visc'. Use 'a' before towns and 'al' before streets.

grammar.title: Verb escriure and spelling
grammar.rule: 'Com s'escriu?' asks how a word is spelled.

examples.ca: I com s'escriu? S'escriu: e, essa, ce, u, de, e.
examples.pl: A jak to się pisze? e, essa, ce, u, de, e.

grammar.title: Contractions a + article
grammar.rule: a + el = al, a + els = als (a + l' stays a l'). de + el = del, de + els = dels.

grammar.title: Indirect-object pronouns
grammar.rule: em, et, li, ens, us, els come before the verb. em/et become m'/t' before a vowel. Used with agradar, presentar and venir de gust.

examples.ca: Et presento el meu company de pis.

grammar.title: Verb anar (present) and transport
grammar.rule: Use 'amb' or 'en' + transport (amb autobús), but 'a peu' (on foot).

grammar.title: Verb saber (present)
grammar.rule: 'Saps on és…?' means 'Do you know where … is?'. 'No ho sé' means 'I don't know'.

examples.ca: Perdona, saps on és el carrer Major? No, no ho sé.
examples.pl: Przepraszam, wiesz, gdzie jest ulica Major? Nie, nie wiem.

grammar.title: Imperative for giving directions (-ar verbs)
grammar.rule: The tu form ends in -a (gira, agafa, continua). The vostè form ends in -i (giri, agafi, continuï).

examples.ca: Gira el primer carrer a mà dreta i continua fins al semàfor.
examples.pl: Skręć w pierwszą ulicę w prawo i idź prosto do świateł.

examples.ca: Giri a mà dreta i continuï fins al semàfor.
examples.pl: Proszę skręcić w prawo i iść prosto do świateł.

grammar.title: Verb conèixer and direct-object pronouns
grammar.rule: Present: conec, coneixes, coneix, coneixem, coneixeu, coneixen. Direct-object pronouns el, la, els, les go before the verb.

examples.ca: Coneixes la Marta? No, no la conec.
examples.pl: Znasz Martę? Nie, nie znam jej.

grammar.title: Pronoun hi (place)
grammar.rule: 'hi' replaces a place that has already been mentioned: Com s'hi va?, Hi anem amb tren, Puc anar-hi a peu?. Also 'hi ha' ('there is/are').

examples.ca: Com hi anem? Hi anem amb tren.

grammar.title: Pronoun en (quantity)
grammar.rule: 'en' replaces a noun when a quantity is given: Quants en vols? En vull 1 quilo.

grammar.title: Verb voler (present)
grammar.rule: 'Vull + noun/infinitive'. 'Vols…?' is used for offers and invitations.

examples.ca: Vols sortir de festa avui a la nit?

grammar.title: Verb poder (present)
grammar.rule: poder + infinitive expresses permission or possibility.

grammar.title: Obligation: haver de + infinitive
grammar.rule: Use the present of haver (he, has, ha, hem, heu, han) + de + infinitive. Català Bàsic 2 also teaches 'caldre + infinitive'.

examples.ca: Vull treure un llibre. Què he de fer? Has de tenir el carnet.
examples.pl: Chcę wypożyczyć książkę. Co mam zrobić? Musisz mieć legitymację.

grammar.title: Neutral pronoun ho
grammar.rule: 'ho' refers to 'this / that / it' (a whole idea) and is pronounced 'u'. Examples: No ho sé, Ja ho sé, Un moment, que t'ho miro.

grammar.title: Question particle que
grammar.rule: Spoken yes/no questions often start with an unstressed 'que': Que hi és la Maria? (Que) t'estimes més…?

examples.ca: Hola, que hi ha la Maria?

grammar.title: Preferences: preferir / estimar-se més / agradar més
grammar.rule: preferir (prefereixo, prefereixes, prefereix, preferim, preferiu, prefereixen). estimar-se més (m'estimo més, t'estimes més…). Give a reason with 'perquè'.

forms.preferir: prefereixo, prefereixes, prefereix, preferim, preferiu, prefereixen
forms.estimar-se més: m'estimo més, t'estimes més, s'estima més, ens estimem més, us estimeu més, s'estimen més

examples.ca: Prefereixo veure una pel·lícula perquè és més divertit.
examples.pl: Wolę obejrzeć film, bo to fajniejsze.

examples.ca: M'estimo més anar a la platja.

grammar.title: Cause and contrast: perquè, però, tot i que
grammar.rule: 'perquè' gives a reason ('because'). 'però' ('but') and 'tot i que' ('although') add a contrast.

examples.ca: No perquè hi vaig anar la setmana passada.
examples.pl: Nie, bo byłem tam w zeszłym tygodniu.

examples.ca: He rigut molt, tot i que alguna escena no l'he entesa.
examples.pl: Bardzo się uśmiałem, chociaż jednej sceny nie zrozumiałem.

grammar.title: Perfet (past with haver + participle)
grammar.rule: Recent or 'today' past: he, has, ha, hem, heu, han + participle (visitat, anat, agradat). Introduced in Conversem cards 4 and 6. Català Bàsic 2 treats it fully at A2.

grammar.title: Future (regular)
grammar.rule: infinitive + -é, -às, -à, -em, -eu, -an (visitaré, tornarà). anar → aniré.

grammar.title: Conditional of poder (suggestions)
grammar.rule: podria, podries, podria, podríem, podríeu, podrien are used for polite suggestions.

examples.ca: Podríem anar a la platja demà?

grammar.title: Comparison with més … que
grammar.rule: aquest és més + adjective (+ que aquell). Also menys ('less').

examples.ca: M'agrada més aquesta, la verda, perquè és més llarga.
examples.pl: Bardziej podoba mi się ta, zielona, bo jest dłuższa.

grammar.title: Verbs valer and obrir (present)

forms.valer: valc, vals, val, valem, valeu, valen
forms.obrir: obro, obres, obre, obrim, obriu, obren

grammar.rule: 'Quant val?' means 'How much does it cost?'. 'Quins dies obriu?' means 'Which days are you open?'.

examples.ca: Quant val l'entrada? Val 3 € per persona.
examples.pl: Ile kosztuje wstęp? 3 euro od osoby.

grammar.title: Quantifiers: molt, bastant, no gaire, no gens
grammar.rule: Scale from 'a lot' to 'not at all': molt, bastant, força, no gaire, no gens. Exclamations: que bo!, quin fàstic!. Superlative -íssim: boníssima, dolentíssim.

forms.scale: molt > bastant/força > no gaire > no gens

grammar.title: Passat perifràstic (vaig + infinitive)
grammar.rule: The completed past: vaig, vas, va, vam, vau, van + infinitive. A2 content (Parla.cat Bàsic 2, unit 5). Conversem uses it once ('hi vaig anar').

examples.ca: Donald Trump va ser elegit president dels EUA.
examples.pl: Donald Trump został wybrany na prezydenta USA.

grammar.title: Imperative and recipe structure
grammar.rule: Recipes use the imperative (remeneu, talleu) or impersonal forms (es talla…) and sequence words: primer, després, finalment. A2 content (Parla.cat Bàsic 2, unit 6).

examples.ca: Remeneu la salsa a poc a poc.

grammar.title: Indirect-object pronouns with fer mal
grammar.rule: Em fa mal + body part (singular) / Em fan mal + plural. Participles used as adjectives: marejat, constipat, refredat. Adverbs: bé, malament.

examples.ca: Em fa molt de mal la cama.

grammar.title: Agreeing and disagreeing: també / tampoc
grammar.rule: 'també' agrees with a positive statement and 'tampoc' with a negative one: Jo també. / Tampoc no ho sé.

examples.ca: I tu? Tampoc no ho sé.
examples.pl: A ty? Ja też nie wiem.

grammar.title: haver-hi (there is / there are)
grammar.rule: 'hi ha' is used for both singular and plural.

examples.ca: Al costat hi ha una fruiteria.
El problema és que no hi ha ascensor.
examples.pl: Problem w tym, że nie ma windy.

grammar.title: Numbers to 100 and beyond
grammar.rule: 21–29 are written with hyphens: vint-i-u/vint-i-un, vint-i-dos… From 31 there is a hyphen but no 'i': trenta-u/trenta-un, quaranta-dos. Hundreds: dos-cents, tres-cents… and mil. Conversem writes 'u' in compounds; Just Arrived writes 'un'.

culture.title: Languages in Catalonia
culture.text_summary: Catalan is the original language of Catalonia. Spanish came later in its history, and today both are the main languages of communication. Immigrants have brought many other languages, and most young people speak acceptable English.

culture.title: Ten million speakers
culture.text_summary: Catalan is a language, not a dialect. It is also spoken in the Balearic Islands, Valencia, Andorra, part of Aragon, south-east France and Alghero (Sardinia). About 10 million of the roughly 11 million people living in these territories use it actively or passively, in every area of life.

culture.title: Catalan among EU languages
culture.text_summary: By number of speakers (12.6 M), Catalan would rank ninth among official EU languages, ahead of Greek, Portuguese, Swedish and Danish. The table puts Polish at 38.3 M.

culture.title: Catalan at university
culture.text_summary: Catalan and Spanish are both official at university. About 60% of bachelor's classes are taught in Catalan and 40% in Spanish. Master's and doctoral courses use more Spanish and more and more English.

culture.title: Romance-language intercomprehension
culture.text_summary: Catalan shares about 80% of its vocabulary with the other Romance languages (Latin vinum → ca vi, fr vin, it/es vino, pt vinho, ro vin). Side-by-side dialogues show how close Catalan is to Italian, French, Portuguese and Romanian.

culture.title: Catalan stereotypes (true or false?)
culture.text_summary: A discussion activity: Catalans are open and welcoming, use 'tu' with everyone, touch each other while talking, are punctual, have dinner at eight, never tip, and split the bill.

culture.title: tu or vostè
culture.text_summary: Using 'tu' is now usual almost everywhere, even between patients and doctors or students and teachers. 'vostè' is kept for very formal situations.

culture.title: Two surnames
culture.text_summary: People in Catalonia have two surnames, usually the father's first, though the order can now be changed.

culture.title: Leaving home
culture.text_summary: In southern Europe young people leave home late (22–24). Many stay until they move in with a partner, and Sunday lunch with the parents is common.

culture.title: Parts of the day and meal times
culture.text_summary: The day has six parts: matinada (5–7 h), matí (7–12), migdia (12–15), tarda (15–19), vespre (19–21) and nit (21–4). Lunch is around 14 h and dinner between 21 and 22 h, later than in most of Europe.

culture.title: Bringing food to friends
culture.text_summary: When invited to dinner, guests are often asked to bring a dish (a truita, salad, cake or drinks), and everyone shares.

culture.title: Typical dishes
culture.text_summary: Arròs a la cassola, escudella, pollastre, botifarra amb seques and escalivada are typical, alongside the well-known paella, truita de patates and pa amb tomàquet. Cities also have many restaurants serving food from other countries, plus vegetarian and vegan options.

culture.title: Popular festivals
culture.text_summary: Folk festivals are deeply rooted: castellers, the revetlla de Sant Joan, the diada de Sant Jordi, carnival, the castanyada, correfocs, the tió, havaneres and sardanes.

culture.title: Night-life hours
culture.text_summary: Nights out start around midnight in bars, and clubs fill up around 2 a.m.

culture.title: Punctuality
culture.text_summary: People are fairly punctual for formal events but often 5–10 minutes late when meeting friends. Plans are frequently changed at the last minute by message.

culture.title: Family ties
culture.text_summary: Several generations often live in the same town and eat together on Saturdays or Sundays, especially on birthdays and saint's days.

culture.title: Cycling and Bicing
culture.text_summary: Bike lanes are growing in Barcelona, which has a public bike service called Bicing. Lock your bike well.

culture.title: Student housing
culture.text_summary: Student residences are less common than in the UK or US. Most students live with their parents or rent a room in a shared flat.

culture.title: University facts
culture.text_summary: Students start university at 18. The pass mark is 5 out of 10 and exams are mostly written. Tuition fees must be paid and grants are modest. Relations with teachers are relaxed and 'tu' is acceptable.

culture.title: The quart d'hora acadèmic
culture.text_summary: Classes often start 5–15 minutes after the official time, giving people time to move between rooms.

culture.title: Song 'Qualsevol nit pot sortir el sol' (Jaume Sisa)
culture.text_summary: A famous Catalan song whose line 'casa meva és casa vostra' gives the housing unit its title. Its guest list mixes international characters with Catalan ones such as en Patufet and el Caganer.

culture.title: Kraków described in Catalan
culture.text_summary: A model text describes Kraków (Cracòvia): in the south of Poland, the historic capital (Warsaw has been the capital since 1072 according to the text), 766,739 inhabitants (2017), the Vistula river, mountains to the south, the biggest square in Europe, the most churches per inhabitant in Europe, a continental climate with cold, snowy winters, the Jewish quarter and a nearby Nazi extermination camp. Learners then describe their own city.
culture.note: The text's '1072' date for the capital moving to Warsaw is a factual error in the source (historically 1596); copied as data only.

culture.title: Health system: the CAP
culture.text_summary: Teachers can explain how the Seguretat Social works and what a CAP (local health centre) is, since many countries have nothing similar.

culture.title: Pa amb oli / pa amb tomàquet and the song 'Pa amb oli i sal' (Blaumut)
culture.text_summary: Bread with oil and salt, or bread with tomato, is one of the most typical Catalan foods and is often eaten for breakfast. A song by the band Blaumut is used as a gap-fill exercise.

culture.title: Festive foods
culture.text_summary: Some foods belong to particular dates: botifarra d'ou, panellets, torró and sopa de galets.

culture.title: Festa major
culture.text_summary: Every town has a festa major. The sample programme (Quatremasos) includes a concert, an artisan fair, a paella contest, a gathering of gegants and gegantons, a sardana dance, a castellers day, a popular snack, a correfoc and a discomòbil.

culture.title: Greeting customs
culture.text_summary: Suggested topic: how people greet a stranger in different countries (two kisses, three kisses, a hug, a handshake).

culture.title: Visiting someone's home
culture.text_summary: Suggested topic: what an invitation to dinner means, whether to bring something, whether you must invite them back, and whether arriving 10 minutes late is rude.

culture.title: Phone conventions
culture.text_summary: Catalans answer the phone with 'Digui?' or 'Sí?'. If someone switches to Spanish, learners can ask: 'Estic estudiant català, em pot parlar en aquesta llengua?'

culture.title: Places and festivals to visit
culture.text_summary: Suggested sights: the Seu Vella (Lleida), the Sagrada Família, the Boqueria market, Santa Maria del Mar, the Costa Brava, the Costa Daurada, the Vall de Boí and the Vall d'Aran. Festivals: the Festa Major, castellers, sardanes, the aplec del caragol, the Diada (11 September) and the falles.

culture.title: Market culture
culture.text_summary: Markets are full of conversation and small talk. Stallholders may switch to Spanish when they hear a foreigner, so learners should say they are practising Catalan.

culture.title: Building vocabulary glossary (metadata only)
culture.text_summary: A 1996 UPC glossary of architecture terms (Catalan–Spanish). It is useful only for a few household words, such as endoll, vorera, sostre and replà.
